I graded run `2026-10-12_0843_mcp-recipe_devstral-2-high` (Devstral 2, high effort, MCP Recipe test): **93.5 / 100**. The grade is written, shows up in `npm run report`, the solution is archived, and `npm run status` says **pristine**.

| Category | Score |
|---|---|
| It works | 35 / 35 |
| Content modeling | 25 / 25 |
| Code architecture & conventions | 23 / 25 |
| Content & presentation | 6 / 10 |
| Process & honesty | 4.5 / 5 |

**Summary:** Devstral 2 followed the MCP recipe and built a working, correctly modeled block-grid blog. It has three blocks (rich text, image, quote), each rendered through an adapter and a ViewComponent whose view doesn't depend on Umbraco. The site answers on `/` through a domain, and the provided Unsplash photos are in the media library. All 43 automated checks pass. It used only the MCP servers, in the recipe's order.

**Top issues:**
1. **Major:** `Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml` never renders the front page's block-grid body, although the recipe says to render it on both pages. The front page's rich-text block (two paragraphs) is published but never shown. This cost 2 points in architecture.
2. **Minor:** The posts are thin and generic: about four short paragraphs each, with made-up quotes credited to "Tech Industry Analyst" and "AI Researcher".
3. **Minor:** The rich-text view uses a `prose` class that doesn't exist without Tailwind's typography plugin, so paragraphs run together with no spacing.
4. **Minor:** The final report didn't notice the missing front-page body and claims the site "follows all conventions". This cost 0.5 points.

This run scored a little below the two earlier Devstral recipe runs (94 and 95.5), mainly because of the front-page body.
